title: llama : deny -sm tensor for arches with moe amax rescaling
body:
## Overview

`llm_arch_supports_sm_tensor` denies `--split-mode tensor` per architecture. The MoE amax rescaling from #30861 builds a `POOL_1D` max reduction with `k = s = ne[0]`, so the pooling window spans the entire matmul row. Under `--split-mode tensor` the MoE intermediate is split along axis 0, which means no device holds a complete row: each one pools over its own slice and gets a partial max. The `handle_pool_1d` split-state case reported `MIRRORED` for that input, but the values are not the same per device, so the claim is false and the rescale is not guaranteed to cancel once the partials are summed.

This removes the `POOL_1D` case from the Meta backend, restoring the previous grouping with the conv and pool ops, and adds `mellum` and `flint` to the deny list next to `mistral4`. Both sites carry a shared `[TAG_MOE_AMAX_SCALE]` marker so the entries can be dropped together when the rescaling goes away.

## Additional information

The graph still applies the rescaling to `cur` and undoes it on the down-projection output; only the tensor-split path is disabled. `test-llama-archs` reported NMSE around `9.6e-08` for `flint` and `9.2e-08` for `mellum` on the meta backend before this change and now skips both, like every other denied architecture. All 534 cases pass.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES
  - Harness: `dsh:llama.cpp`
  - Hardware: `MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB`
  - Model: [ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF)
  - Stats: `◷ 53.2m · ⚙ 5.1m · ↑ 282k · ↓ 111k · ≡ 299 · ⌨ 31`
